definitions.explanation: A Japanese cooking method and the resulting dish where ingredients are simmered in a seasoned broth of soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and sake until the liquid is reduced and the flavors are absorbed.

examples.japanese: {魚|さかな}の{煮付|につ}けを{作|つく}る。
{今日|きょう}の{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}はカレイの{煮付|につ}けだ。
{祖母|そぼ}の{煮付|につ}けは{醤油|しょうゆ}と{砂糖|さとう}の{味|あじ}がしっかり{染|し}みていて{絶品|ぜっぴん}だった。
examples.english: My grandmother's simmered dish was exquisite, with the soy sauce and sugar flavors thoroughly soaked in.

notes: One of the fundamental Japanese home cooking techniques. The most common combination is {魚|さかな}の{煮付|につ}け (simmered fish), especially with flat white fish like カレイ (flounder) or {金目鯛|きんめだい} (splendid alfonsino). {煮物|にもの} is the broader term for simmered dishes in general, while {煮付|につ}け specifically implies cooking until the broth is reduced and concentrated. The verb form is {煮付|につ}ける.
